chapter: Frankie Newton and the Boston Savoy
title: Frankie Newton's politics and the New Masses
summary: Newton was to the left of Hentoff, wrote for the New Masses, and both ended up on lists.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Tell me as much as you can remember about Frankie Newton, specifically, where was he politically?

Politically he was to the left of me. I was pretty liberal, but having read Darkness at Noon by Arthur Koestler and got to know what Stalinism was like, I was a total anti-Communist. Frankie was so idealistic in some respects, but so pragmatic in terms of the effects of Jim Crow etc., that he was, I think – entranced isn’t the word – influenced by the rhetoric of people on what I consider the far right – the far – well, far left, far right, it’s all to me the same religion.

He wrote for The New Masses and that kind of publication and got himself on various lists. So did I, as a matter of fact. My FBI file has been very useful to me, because I don’t have that good a memory.
